name: Evidence spine
useWhen: A decision needs traceable source material.
strategy: Make the source a stable reading spine; attach proposed actions to exact evidence.
signature: Use a shared alignment axis and small source anchors; reveal detail where it is cited.
mobile: One source and decision at a time, with a clear return to the queue.
risk: Weak when source reading is secondary. Never invent evidence or confidence.

name: Delta first
useWhen: The user must understand what will change.
strategy: Lead with the change, then expose original context and consequences.
signature: Let additions, removals, and unchanged context create hierarchy; use words as well as color.
mobile: Stack paired fields with persistent Original and Proposed labels.
risk: Avoid for unrelated objects or changes with no meaningful baseline.

name: Triage lanes
useWhen: A large queue contains different next actions.
strategy: Group by actual work state or decision type, then show the next useful action.
signature: Give each lane a clear verb and distinct content rhythm, within one shared visual system.
mobile: Use a compact lane selector and a readable list, preserving counts and selection.
risk: Do not invent priority scores. Avoid arbitrary categories or hiding unassigned work.

name: Object workbench
useWhen: The user works deeply on one object.
strategy: Keep the object stable while context and tools change around it.
signature: Build one distinctive object view; align tools to the part they affect.
mobile: Move secondary tools into labelled drawers; keep the object and primary action visible.
risk: Avoid a three-pane layout when the object does not need sustained attention.

name: Preview then commit
useWhen: A configuration has consequences the user needs to predict.
strategy: Show a live, honest preview beside a short set of controls; separate draft from commit.
signature: Make each input visibly affect the same product scene, with clear saved and unsaved states.
mobile: Alternate between controls and preview with preserved input and an explicit commit action.
risk: A fabricated preview creates false trust. Explain unsupported effects.

name: Time and state
useWhen: Users need both current truth and how it changed.
strategy: Pair a calm current snapshot with a selective event trail.
signature: Use time spacing and event structure to show meaningful changes; keep current values prominent.
mobile: Lead with current state, then a vertically readable event trail with date anchors.
risk: Avoid decorative timelines for unordered content; separate event time from report time.

name: Relationship map
useWhen: Relationships or dependencies determine the next action.
strategy: Make connections spatial and provide a linked list for exact lookup.
signature: Give position a stable meaning; reveal one relevant path rather than every edge.
mobile: Use the linked list and a focused path view, preserving the same selection.
risk: Avoid when proximity has no meaning. A canvas requires keyboard and list alternatives.

name: Mechanism scene
useWhen: A product is easier to understand by seeing how it works.
strategy: Turn one real product mechanism into the central scene, with a short evidence-led story.
signature: Use purposeful scale, typography, and a single visual transformation tied to the mechanism.
mobile: Retell the scene in a linear sequence; preserve the same proof and call to action.
risk: Do not invent metrics, logos, or capabilities. Avoid a decorative mock dashboard.

name: Constraint composer
useWhen: The user must balance a few clear constraints.
strategy: Make constraints editable and show their effect on a valid outcome.
signature: Use a compact visual model of remaining capacity or tradeoffs, with precise labels.
mobile: Use sequential constraint controls plus a persistent result summary.
risk: Use only real calculation rules. Never imply an optimum without a defined objective.
